page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-48 is a compute-focused virtual server configuration built on the Intel Xeon x86_64 architecture. It provides 48 vCPUs across 24 dedicated physical cores with two threads per core running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware AES cryptographic acceleration. Memory is provisioned at 48.0 GB, establishing a 1:1 gigabyte-to-vCPU ratio. This configuration contains no local storage and includes zero GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks establish average multi-core processing alongside constrained single-core throughput. Stress-ng records 44,617.16 in multi-core compute tests, while single-core processing scores 1,410.49. In Geekbench testing, the instance registers 1,161.0 for single-core and 10,859.0 for multi-core performance, achieving 30,076.0 in Clang software compilation and 30,774.0 in ray tracing. Memory bandwidth tests yield 153.47 GB/sec read and 79.98 GB/sec write on large 256 MB blocks. Compression benchmarks mirror the core scaling profile, where multi-threaded bzip3 decompression processes 60.51 GB/sec compared to 23.8 GB/sec for single-threaded gzip compression.

From an architectural standpoint, n2-highcpu-48 trades memory capacity for processor density. The allocation of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU limits its suitability for large in-memory databases or caching systems, although Redis SET operations achieve 41.27 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaches 29.33 GB/sec. Large language model text generation remains low at 53.69 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated acceleration. Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-48 is best matched for parallelized compute tasks, software build pipelines, CI/CD jobs, batch data transformation, and multi-threaded web serving.
